reason: The text demonstrates that multiple actors across social strata exercise agency. While the Egyptian king (a leader) clearly acts with agency—planning a strategy and commanding the oppression—the Israelite people, who are not leaders, also demonstrate agency through their demographic response. The passage states 'וְכַאֲשֶׁר יְעַנּוּ אֹתוֹ כֵּן יִרְבֶּה' ('the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied'), indicating that the Israelites continue to grow and thrive despite efforts to suppress them. This is an active response that contradicts the notion that only leaders possess agency. The narrative structure itself shows the Israelites as agents in their own story, not merely passive subjects of the king's will.
